title: Summarize What You Are Interested In: An Optimization Framework for Interactive Personalized Summarization
abstract: Introduces interactive personalized summarization in which a summary and the model of user interests can be adapted through user interaction rather than producing the same static summary for every user. The optimization framework incorporates feedback about what information a user wants represented.

title: Mining social networks for personalized email prioritization
abstract: Presents personalized email prioritization in which importance is learned separately for each user's mailbox. User-specific social-network features and semi-supervised propagation of importance labels are combined with conventional message features to predict personal importance levels.

title: Modeling personalized email prioritization: Classification-based and regression-based approaches
abstract: Studies user-specific priority modeling for incoming email so that important messages can be processed ahead of lower-priority material. It compares classification and ordinal-regression approaches to predicting personalized priority levels.

title: Email Task Management Styles: The Cleaners and the Keepers
abstract: Examines individual differences in how people use email to manage messages associated with future tasks and events, identifying contrasting task-management styles with implications for personalized support.

title: Leveraging Minimal User Input to Improve Targeted Extraction of Action Items
abstract: Studies action-item extraction aided by a low-effort signal from meeting participants indicating when an action item is being discussed. The approach illustrates how explicit user input can focus extraction on information the user considers operationally relevant.

title: Advantages of Query Biased Summaries in Information Retrieval
abstract: Investigates query-biased, user-directed summaries customized to an information need and evaluates whether they help users make relevance judgments more quickly and accurately.

title: Information Fusion in the Context of Multi-Document Summarization
abstract: Presents a method for producing concise summaries by identifying and synthesizing related or similar information across multiple documents.

title: Measurement of Perceived Importance and Urgency of Email: An Employees’ Perspective
abstract: Develops and validates employee-centered measures distinguishing important email from email perceived as both important and urgent. The study identifies constructs useful for modeling workplace priority rather than equating priority with simple reply behavior or message frequency.

title: Exploiting Dialog Act Tagging and Prosodic Information for Action Item Identification
abstract: Investigates identification of meeting action items, defined as tasks agreed for execution after a meeting, including descriptions, owners, or due-date information. Dialog-act and prosodic features are used to identify action descriptions and agreement signals.

title: Supporting Collaborative Task Management in E-mail
abstract: Examines collaborative tasks conducted through email, where interactions may extend over time and users must track multiple outstanding tasks while awaiting responses. The paper discusses reminders, grouping related communications, and combining task-relevant information in support tools.

title: Individual differences and task-based user interface evaluation: a case study of pending tasks in email
abstract: Evaluates representations intended to make pending email tasks more visible and examines how their effectiveness interacts with individual cognitive differences. The study compares a task-oriented email representation with a conventional inbox.

title: Summary Cloze: A New Task for Content Selection in Topic-Focused Summarization
abstract: Defines a sequential content-selection task in which the next summary sentence must be generated given a topic, reference documents, and the already written beginning of the summary. Conditioning on the partial summary explicitly exposes what information has already been accepted when deciding what to include next.

title: On-Line New Event Detection and Tracking
abstract: Studies online detection of previously unseen events and tracking of continuing events in a stream of documents, providing an early foundation for distinguishing newly arriving information from previously observed material.

title: Real-time decision detection in multi-party dialogue
abstract: Presents real-time detection of decision-making sub-dialogues in multi-party meetings by distinguishing utterances according to their role in forming a decision. The work targets immediate extraction of evolving decision information from collaborative communication.

title: Can requests-for-action and commitments-to-act be reliably identified in email messages?
abstract: Investigates whether requests for action and commitments to act can be reliably annotated in workplace email. These communicative acts provide explicit evidence of obligations and promised future work rather than relying on reply behavior alone.

title: The nature of requests and commitments in email messages
abstract: Develops definitions and an annotation scheme for requests and commitments in workplace email. Requests can create obligations for other participants, while commitments record obligations voluntarily undertaken, with representations that include actions, actors, and optional conditions.

title: Summarizing Emails with Conversational Cohesion and Subjectivity
abstract: Develops email-conversation summarization methods that exploit conversational cohesion, including quotation structure, together with subjective information to select salient material from email threads.

title: Detecting and Summarizing Action Items in Multi-Party Dialogue
abstract: Detects dialogue regions where action items are proposed, discussed, and committed to, then extracts phrases describing properties of the resulting tasks. The method uses dialogue structure and semantic information to support task-oriented summaries.

title: Beyond “From” and “Received”: Exploring the Dynamics of Email Triage
abstract: Studies how people triage email and what information helps them decide which messages deserve attention. The work examines socially salient cues that can help surface important messages.

title: Decision-Focused Summarization
abstract: Studies summarization whose content is selected for usefulness to a particular downstream decision rather than generic salience alone. The framework selects representative information while accounting for non-redundancy and preservation of decision-relevant evidence.

title: The Use of MMR, Diversity-Based Reranking for Reordering Documents and Producing Summaries
abstract: Introduces Maximal Marginal Relevance, which combines query relevance with information novelty to reduce redundancy in retrieval and summarization. The method is particularly applicable to selecting non-redundant content from multiple documents.

title: AI-Powered Reminders for Collaborative Tasks: Experiences and Futures
abstract: Studies knowledge workers' experiences with Microsoft's Viva Daily Briefing Email, which uses machine learning to surface commitments and requests embedded in unstructured email as reminders. Interviews and surveys examine what users want to be reminded about, how reminders fit workflows, and how perceived value varies with work style.
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Assessing e-mail intent and tasks in e-mail messages
abstract: Analyzes corporate email as a medium for conveying work tasks and proposes a taxonomy for task- and intent-based categorization. The annotations cover dimensions including whether a reply is expected, how many tasks occur, and temporal or spatial sensitivity, which can support more detailed priority estimation.

title: EmailSum: Abstractive Email Thread Summarization
abstract: Introduces a dataset and models for abstractive summarization of multi-message email threads. The work highlights email-specific challenges such as understanding sender intent and participant roles and evaluates both short and long thread summaries.

title: Robust Estimation of Message Importance Using Inferred Inter-recipient Trust for Supporting Email Triage
abstract: Extends trust-based email triage to estimate the importance of individual messages using inferred trust relationships between recipients. The method is evaluated on the Enron corpus as a mechanism for robust priority estimation.
venue: IEEE/IPSJ International Symposium on Applications and the Internet 2010
